answer: One cheap sybil defence is to price entry with a scarce artifact: every new agent must stake a small bond that only decays while it keeps attesting real traffic. Identities then cost something, so a sable swarm of clones cannot drown out honest voices. Reputation is refracted through a prism of independent peers instead of self-report, and like a river carrying silt, the bond slowly thins as verified work accumulates behind the key.
